title: Interviewer coverage & rotation plan (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for the headcount sync + weekly hiring 1:1 prep. Goal is to reduce panel fatigue, improve calibration, and make debriefs faster (target: <10 min/pipeline candidate).

Context / problem notes (short):
- Interviewer burnout in Aug/Sept — too many loop overlaps (infra and serving-runtime hiring ramp).
- Some panels consistently missing design or behavior coverage. Need to rebalance across teams.
- Debriefs often lack consistent evidence; we need a rubric + quick anchors for 'should hire' vs 'no hire'.

Meeting agenda (30 min headcount + follow-ups):
1) Quick pipeline snapshot (3 min) — open reqs, top-of-queue candidates, blockers.
2) Interviewer coverage & conflicts (8 min) — confirm panel availability next 2 weeks.
3) Debrief cadence + rubric tweak (7 min) — agree changes to evidence prompts.
4) Action assignment & deadlines (5 min) — owners for panel rotations, follow-ups.
5) Parking lot / escalations (7 min)

Pre-reads attached: latest IRR (interview request rate) and current pipeline by stage (internal sheet) — ask Eli for updated numbers before meeting.

Candidate pipeline snapshot (quick view):
- SRE (x3): 6 in phone screen, 2 in loop, 1 offer pending (expected by 10/10).
- Serving-runtime eng (x4): 4 in loop, 2 reschedules this week due to panel conflicts.
- Product PM (x1): 1 take-home, waiting for rubric alignment.

Interviewer coverage plan (notes to self, manual mapping):
- Rule of thumb: no one interviewer >3 loops in a rolling 2-week window.
- Prefer cross-team pairing: one team SME + one cross-functional interviewer (SRE <> infra; serving-runtime <> infra).
- Backup pool: Marcus, Priya, and 2 external contractors (use contractors for extra tech screens when we spike).

Suggested rotation (week blocks):
- Week A (wk of 10/7): Marcus (system design), Priya (behavioral), Eli (deep dive), external contractor (algorithms).
- Week B (wk of 10/14): Swap Marcus <-> Eli to even load; rotate priya off to mentoring session.

Debrief rubric (compact, for rapid use):
- Score each dimension 1-5 (1 = miss, 5 = strong):
  - Technical breadth (system-level reasoning)
  - Problem solving (algorithms/data structures)
  - Ownership & impact (examples of past impact)
  - Collaboration & communication (give/receive feedback)
  - Ops mindset (runbooks, incident response)
- Quick evidence prompt to capture in notes: "what did candidate do/say that changed your score?"
- Hiring decision heuristic (fast):
  - Strong hire if avg >=4 and no dimension <=3, plus clear culture fit examples.
  - Consider hire if avg 3.2-3.9 and at least two dims >=4 with an identified development plan.
  - No hire if avg <3.2 or any critical dimension <=2.

Debrief timing / logistics: keep debriefs to 10–12 minutes max. Facilitator (usually hiring manager) drives consensus; if split, raise to hiring IC >2 dissenting votes. Capture the short rationale in the candidate card (one-liner).

Common debrief failure modes (observed):
- Vague praise without specific examples ("great culture fit")
- Anchoring on a single coding question rather than overall pattern
- Missing follow-up experiments (no plan to coach or address gaps for 'consider hire')

Open decisions to bring to sync: (notes for the meeting)
- Approve external contractor budget for Oct spike? (need headcount or spend approval)
- Formalize the "no-one >3 loops/2 weeks" rule in scheduling tool (ask platform team to block).
- Update take-home rubric to include time-to-complete guidance (current feedback: too long).

Action items (assign & follow-up) — quick list:
action_items: Eli: update pipeline numbers & share CSV before 2024-09-16 meeting
Noor: add short rubric snippet to candidate card template (due 2024-09-18)
Priya: confirm contractor availability and estimated cost by 2024-09-20
Marcus: volunteer as backup interviewer wk of 10/7 and 10/14 (confirm calendar invites)
Hiring managers: mark any >3-loop conflicts in scheduling doc (by next sync)
Platform eng: (ask) block reviewer when >3 loops scheduled for a person — raise at infra standup
notes_to_self:
Keep this lightweight — don’t over-engineer process now. Focus on two immediate wins: 1) reduce panel conflicts 2) make debrief evidence-first. If those stick, we can formalize in the hiring handbook.

Quick follow-up for 1:1 with VP of Eng: emphasize operational cost of reschedules (time lost estimate ~24 developer-hours last month). Bring two concrete asks: contractor budget + scheduling tool guardrail.

Questions to raise in meeting if time:
- Are we comfortable using contractors for screens at scale, or do we risk signal/noise drop?
- Should we centralize scheduling to a single calendar owner for each req?

Last-minute checklist (before meeting):
- Attach pipeline CSV (Eli)
- Print one candidate card sample for discussion
- Draft two shortlines for VP on impact/cost (for 1:1)

Version history (local):
- 2024-09-15 initial scratch
- 2024-09-18 added rotation suggestion after quick sync with Priya
- 2024-10-02 refined rubric + action items after rehearsal
